content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments and build tooling. Hands-on experience with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, plus personal experience operating a k3s homelab and provisioning Hetzner VPS infrastructure with Terraform. Known for improving pipeline performance, documenting CI workflows and working across QA and product teams. Preparing for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam, scheduled for January 2027.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal project), Argo CD
Containers & platforms: Kubernetes (namespace-level deployments), k3s, Linux
Monitoring & data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Languages & scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Other: Git, Ansible (basic), AWS (EC2 and S3 fundamentals through personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end testing; the improvement also reduced monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Built short-lived, per-merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; they are removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built Python tooling to collect CI test results into PostgreSQL and Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
- Authored an internal guide to how the CI system works, used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd Line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Set up a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured and professional CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It uses clear headings, concise bullets, measurable outcomes and relevant project evidence. The strongest content is the quantified CI improvement, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes namespace-level work, observability project and homelab. The main content limitation is that the CV presents several infrastructure capabilities without clearly separating professional production experience from personal learning, although it does disclose this in some places. It also does not explicitly demonstrate systems design, security awareness, stakeholder leadership or technical proposal ownership at the level expected for this contractor role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, conventional text formatting, strong keyword coverage and no apparent parsing obstacles. It includes relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Linux, AWS, PostgreSQL and TLS. ATS alignment would improve if supported terminology such as infrastructure as code, cloud infrastructure, observability, certificate management, system design and technical documentation were used more explicitly. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS or production AWS experience because the candidate information does not support them. AI screening may recognise the DevOps transition and infrastructure potential, but may rank the CV below candidates with stronger Terraform/Terragrunt, AWS, networking and production operations evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows a credible junior-to-mid DevOps/platform profile, particularly for CI/CD, test infrastructure, Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, Linux, observability and automation. It aligns with the company's engineering-led, collaborative and ownership-oriented culture through pipeline ownership, cross-team work, documentation, mentoring and measurable improvements. It does not yet present a strong match for a contractor expected to shape cloud architecture from the start and take it to production. The candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud infrastructure, mTLS, broader network design, production on-call and full system-design ownership. AWS is shown only at fundamentals/personal-learning level. There is no IoT, automotive or remote-device integration evidence. The Java experience provides a limited JVM-related match, while Linux is clearly supported; virtual-machine experience is not shown.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, make the professional-versus-personal scope explicit while positioning the candidate accurately for the role. Replace the current summary with wording such as: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including 2 years owning CI/CD and test infrastructure for three product teams. Professional experience includes GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, ephemeral environments and observability tooling. Personal infrastructure work includes a k3s homelab, Argo CD, Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure and Prometheus/Grafana/Loki. Strong in automation, analytical pipeline optimisation, technical documentation and cross-team enablement; transitioning into a full-time platform engineering role." This avoids implying production cloud or cluster ownership.
2. In the Technical Skills section, label experience scope more precisely. Change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project)" and change "AWS (EC2 and S3 fundamentals through personal learning)" to "AWS: EC2 and S3 fundamentals (personal learning)". This makes the CV more credible for human and AI screening.
3. In the Odrava Health Software experience, strengthen the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence using only supported facts. Add a bullet such as: "Owned CI/CD improvements across three product teams (~25 developers), documenting the CI workflow for onboarding and enabling QA and product teams to review features in per-merge-request environments." This better supports the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along without claiming formal architecture leadership.
4. In the Technical Skills section, add the supported ATS terms "infrastructure as code," "observability," "certificate management" and "TLS" in truthful context. For example: "Infrastructure as code: Terraform (personal Hetzner project); Helm" and "Observability and certificate management: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, cert-manager, TLS." Do not list mTLS, Terragrunt or network design because they are not supported by the candidate information.
5. In the Selected Infrastructure Project section, clarify the scope of the TLS work. Change "cert-manager for TLS" to "cert-manager for TLS certificate management" if that accurately reflects the project, while retaining the existing Traefik ingress detail. Do not describe this as mutual TLS or secure train-to-cloud communication.

MINOR ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise "Built Python tooling to collect CI test results into PostgreSQL and Grafana dashboards" to "Built Python tooling that collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and exposed flaky-test metrics through Grafana dashboards." This is more precise and uses the job's observability terminology.
7. In the Selected Infrastructure Project section, make the infrastructure-as-code result clearer by revising the Terraform bullet to: "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used basic Ansible configuration; this was personal infrastructure work, not production company cloud infrastructure." This prevents overinterpretation while preserving relevant evidence.
8. In the Professional Summary or a short "Selected Strengths" line below it, add the supported communication and analytical evidence: "Analytical approach demonstrated through pipeline profiling, a 63% pipeline-time reduction, flaky-test analysis and CI workflow documentation used for onboarding." This directly reinforces the ad's analytical-thinking requirement without making an unsupported claim of senior technical leadership.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible CV with a clear DevOps/platform transition narrative, quantified achievements, relevant project evidence, and transparent qualification of personal versus production infrastructure. The strongest content is the 63% pipeline-time reduction, 30% CI runner-cost reduction, ephemeral-environment implementation, and reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The document is professional and easy to scan. The main content weakness is some repetition in the Odrava experience section and a slightly broad skills section that could be more tightly prioritised for this infrastructure role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, simple text formatting, conventional date and role structures, and strong keyword coverage for GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, Python, Bash, and AWS. Quantified accomplishment bullets also improve both recruiter and AI-screening performance. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to high for general DevOps or platform roles, but lower for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain supported evidence or keywords for Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, security awareness, or virtual machines. Do not add those terms as competencies unless supported by actual experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on CI/CD infrastructure, Kubernetes-based environment deployment, observability, automation, analytical optimisation, documentation, and cross-team enablement. It also provides credible supporting evidence for Linux, TLS certificate management, AWS fundamentals, and a JVM-related testing background. The candidate's infrastructure experience is primarily test infrastructure, namespace-level Kubernetes work, personal k3s infrastructure, and a personal Hetzner Terraform project rather than production cloud-platform ownership. The candidate material does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, production AWS or other major-cloud operation, virtual machines, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, or explicit systems architecture/system-design ownership. Practical security awareness is also not clearly evidenced. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording. The strongest truthful alignment is the candidate's ownership of technical CI/CD improvements, ability to bring QA and product teams into per-merge-request environments, analytical pipeline optimisation, and clear technical documentation.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, remove the duplicated final bullet beginning "Owned CI/CD improvements across three product teams" because the same ownership and onboarding information is already covered in the first and seventh bullets. Replace it with a more specific stakeholder-impact statement using existing evidence, for example: "Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge through per-merge-request environments, and documented the CI workflow for team onboarding." This preserves the strongest collaboration evidence without repetition.

2. In the Technical Skills section, merge the separate "Infrastructure & CI/CD" and "Infrastructure as code" categories to reduce duplication. Use a structure such as: "CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project), Argo CD." Keep the personal-project qualifier attached to Terraform so the scope remains accurate.

3. In the Professional Summary, make the production-versus-personal scope even more immediately clear by changing "Professional experience includes GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, ephemeral environments and observability tooling" to "Professional experience includes GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, ephemeral environments and test observability; personal infrastructure work includes k3s, Argo CD, Terraform and Prometheus/Grafana/Loki." This improves credibility for a contractor role involving cloud infrastructure ownership.

4. In the Selected Infrastructure Project section, add the supported implementation detail that the Hetzner VPS infrastructure was provisioned with Terraform and configured with basic Ansible, rather than leaving this only in the final explanatory sentence. For example: "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and applied basic Ansible configuration; this was personal infrastructure work, not production company cloud infrastructure." This gives ATS and recruiters a clearer project-level Terraform match without overstating experience.

5. In the Technical Skills section, change "AWS: EC2 and S3 fundamentals (personal learning)" to "AWS: EC2 and S3 fundamentals (personal learning; no production AWS experience)" if space permits. This is optional but makes the scope of the AWS keyword unambiguous and consistent with the CV's otherwise strong transparency.
